title: Low-degree learner work bound
statement: Let $\omega$ be a positive rational number with $2\le\omega$, let $n,k$ be natural numbers, and let $0<\delta\le 1/2$. Suppose a linear solver backend has a certificate for exponent $\omega$: for some natural-number coefficient function, its work on every finite system of linear equations over $\mathbb F_2$ is bounded by that coefficient times $b^{\lceil\omega d\rceil}$ whenever the number of variables is at most $D b^d$, the number of equations is at most $R b^d$, and $b>0$. For any sample of size $m=2^{k-c}(M+F)$, where $c=\lceil\omega k/(\omega+1)\rceil$, $M$ is the number of monomials in $n$ variables of degree at most $k-c$, and $F=\lceil 2/\delta\rceil$ rounded up to the next power of two in the sense $F=\lceil\log_2(2/\delta)\rceil$ as encoded by the failure-bit count, the work of the backend polynomial learner on that sample is at most $C(n+1)^c$, where $C$ is its specified coefficient formed from the certificate, the degree, and the learning parameter.
hypotheses_covered: A linear solver backend and an exponent certificate for it
The certificate supplies a natural-number coefficient function and the stated work bound for all finite equation systems satisfying its variable, row, and positive-base bounds
The samples are indexed by the stated finite sample count and take values in the sign cube times the sign set
caveat: The statement uses several upstream constructions whose informal descriptions are placeholders. The failure-bit count is $\operatorname{clog}_2(\lceil 2/\delta\rceil)$, and the learner coefficient is defined explicitly from the monomial count, row coefficient, and certificate; the prose above summarizes these constructions rather than giving their full expansions.
